facts: [F1] Translation and duality ([[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]], [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]): exactness, biadjunction and block projections for the residue functors.
uses: 2.1 **The operator relations and dual mates.** The operators $x_j,T_j$ are natural endomorphisms of the tensor functors, so the relations of step 1.1 restrict to simultaneous generalized residue components whenever those components are defined. Taking mates under the tensor/block biadjunction transfers the operator identities to the reverse functors, with the dual-Casimir shift $-n-i$ of step 1.2. The nilpotence and identification of these components with block projections are verified after constructing the flags. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

3.1 **Eigencomponents on all objects.** Projectives have finite standard flags, and tensoring their flags with either finite factor gives the flags of step 2.2. On a chosen block component the Casimir differs from its indicated scalar by an operator zero on every flag section, so a power bounded by the flag length annihilates that component. Distinct scalars give distinct changed multisets. Every finite-length object is a quotient of a finite sum of these projectives; naturality of $x$ and exactness of both projections extend the block/eigencomponent identification and nilpotence to all objects. Apply this successively to each tensor place to obtain the natural affine-Hecke action on repeated residue functors, with each $x_j-i$ locally nilpotent. [F1, F3, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

claim:
Assume AC. Work in genuine type-$A$ parabolic category $\mathcal O$ for
$\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its fixed Borel. Its column Levi has ordered
blocks of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. All entries in column $j$ lie in
$c_j+\mathbb Z$, where the original admissibility condition is
$c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z\Rightarrow c_j=c_k$. Use the source highest-weight
convention $\eta_i=a_i+i-1$ and half-sum
$\rho_i=(N+1-2i)/2$, with the column reading prescribed by the source Borel.
For each occurring entry coset $\kappa$ retain its columns in their original
order. Fix an order on the finite set of cosets; no order on $\mathbb C$ is used.

Subject to the local HC tensor-projective comparison stated in [F1], stable
sorting of the coordinates by $\kappa$ gives an exact, complex-linear
equivalence of the genuine parabolic categories, carrying each ordinary
Verma label by the dot permutation and carrying the corresponding generalized
standard, simple head and projective cover. On each linkage block, the sorted
category is equivalent to the product of the corresponding parabolic blocks
for $\mathfrak{gl}_{N_\kappa}$, where
$N_\kappa=\sum_{j\in\kappa}q_j$. Product means the abelian category generated
by finite presentations of outer tensor products, equivalently modules over
the tensor product of the finite block endomorphism algebras.

For the original pyramid with $n$ rows put $n_\kappa=\max_{j\in\kappa}q_j$.
The component integral entry dictionary is exactly
$$a_i^{\mathrm{int}}=a_i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa,\qquad m_j=q_j-n_\kappa,\qquad \inf I_\kappa=1-n_\kappa.$$
Thus $m_j+1-\inf I_\kappa=q_j$, with the original nonincreasing retained
heights and charges. For the admitted-ground subcategories, where each original entry has a
nonnegative integral difference from its own ground entry, this dictionary
lands in the bounded-below admitted integral component models of [F4]. For
other genuine parabolic blocks it records the integral weight/coset
dictionary and the trace shift, without asserting membership in that fixed
admitted cut. If the component follows $B_\kappa$ sorted coordinates, its
Levi highest weight and the integral highest weight differ by the scalar
trace-character shift
$$\delta_\kappa=B_\kappa+c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa.$$
This shift is a Lie algebra character and requires no integrality of
$c_\kappa$. Singular repeated-entry linkage blocks are included. The original
complex origins, component entry multisets and their scalar centres remain
recorded; different complex cosets are not merged into one integral block.

Sorting commutes coherently with finite tensoring and its invariant Casimir
and permutation maps. The separated product decomposition is blockwise and
does not assert that unrestricted tensoring is componentwise. The proof gives
its actual filtration and block-projection comparison. Choices of sorting
word with the same stable permutation yield the natural comparison fixed on
the chosen reference highest vector and its tensor-projective presentations.
facts: [F1] The local tensor-projective comparison [[lem-nonintegral-harish-chandra-tensor-projective-comparison]]: for a regular weight $\lambda$ decreasing within each integral shifted-coordinate coset, finite integral-coordinate tensors $E\otimes\Delta_\lambda$ and their direct summands give projective generators of $\mathcal O_{\lambda+\mathbb Z^N}$; for finite $E,F$ their Hom spaces are naturally $(E^*\otimes F\otimes U_{\chi_\lambda})^{\mathfrak g}$, with evaluation and composition. Its same all-weight Duflo input is required for $s\cdot\lambda$ after a distinct-coset adjacent swap. The all-weight action isomorphism is supplied through that local HC lemma; the present proof uses its Hom comparison at both regular reference weights and does not reprove the Duflo theorem.

[F4] Genuine parabolic modules and the admitted integral component convention: [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]], [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], [[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]. Only the Levi-integrable simple criterion, Serre property, largest generalized-Verma quotient and the explicit integral charge/height convention are consumed. The proof below constructs the nonintegral product rather than importing integral highest-weight conclusions for arbitrary complex labels.
uses: 5.1 Choose regular coset-dominant $\lambda$ in the weight-coset category. Crossing distinct cosets preserves each coset's internal order, so $s\cdot\lambda$ meets the same regular coset-dominance hypotheses; its central character equals $\chi_\lambda$. For a generator map encoded by $t\in(E^*\otimes F\otimes U_\chi)^{\mathfrak g}$, its action is the finite sum of finite-tensor matrix entries followed by enveloping operators on $\Delta_\lambda$. The invariant matrix map commutes with the total $F$ on the tensor modules, so its unique localized extension agrees with the same enveloping-operator formula under the tensor localization of step 4.1. Passing to the quotient, twisting and applying the matrices of step 4.1 transforms $t$ by simultaneous Weyl conjugation in its three factors. Each $t$ lies in a finite adjoint submodule, so that conjugation is $\exp(E_{\mathrm{diag}})\exp(-F_{\mathrm{diag}})\exp(E_{\mathrm{diag}})$ and fixes $t$, since its diagonal $\mathfrak g$-action is zero. Thus $T_s$ induces exactly the common Hom identification of [F1], respecting composition and identity. The scalar from step 3.1 is the same on all generators $X\otimes\Delta_\lambda$, so it cancels on every generator Hom space; an arbitrary unnormalized scalar is not treated as a literal equality of highest vectors. [F1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Every object has a finite presentation by finite direct sums and summands of the generators in [F1]. Exactness and steps 3.1–4.1 show that its $T_s$ image is the cokernel of a map between target generators, hence belongs to the target category $\mathcal O$. Step 5.1 identifies all generator maps. Every target presentation therefore lifts, proving essential surjectivity. Applying Hom from a generator to a source presentation and its target presentation gives identical cokernel diagrams, since those generators are projective; applying Hom from a presented object gives identical kernel diagrams. This proves full faithfulness on all objects. Idempotents are preserved and reflected by the generator Hom identification, so summands cause no gap. Consequently $T_s$ is an exact category equivalence, established on actual maps and presentations. [F1, F2, F5, step 2.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 Compose these swaps in a stable bubble sort by the fixed coset order. Each swap crosses different cosets; none permutes indices inside a coset. The composite sends $\Delta_\eta$ to $\Delta_{w\cdot\eta}$ and therefore sends its unique simple head to $L(w\cdot\eta)$. It transports projective covers by exact equivalence and essentiality. Every original column consists entirely of one coset; stable sorting retains its coordinates as a consecutive block and retains their internal order. At the end, the original Levi simple roots are therefore positive simple roots of the sorted column Levi. Their highest-weight integral-dominance pairings are unchanged. By the actual Levi simple criterion and Serre property of [F4], the composite and its inverse restrict to the full parabolic subcategories. Because generalized Vermas are the largest parabolic-finite quotients of ordinary Vermas, their quotient universal property is transported, giving the claimed generalized-standard labels as modules. No intermediate swap is asserted to preserve an intermediate parabolic subcategory. [F4, step 3.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 The coherent comparison of two sorting paths can be made on tensor-projective generators. Each path has the common [F1] Hom matrix identification of step 5.1; their final Weyl representatives differ at most by a diagonal torus matrix when they induce the same coordinate permutation. Diagonal simultaneous action again fixes invariant matrices. Their reference-standard highest lines admit a unique comparison after fixing its nonzero scalar; tensor it with $X$ for every generator and summand. The equality on generator Hom matrices makes these comparisons natural, and taking presentation cokernels extends them uniquely to all objects, independently of a presentation by full faithfulness. Comparisons for three paths compose because they coincide on the normalized reference generator and its tensor presentations. This proves the stated normalization and coherence, without asserting an unnormalized inverse-twist or braid identity. [F1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra, step 7.1]

12.1 Induction and radical invariants are adjoint, and step 10.1 identifies the latter with $S$. Their unit is PBW's top-section isomorphism $X\to S(R(X))$. For the counit $R(S(M))\to M$, applying exact $S$ gives this identity, so its kernel and cokernel have zero top section; both are finite-length objects of $C$ and vanish by detection in step 10.1. Hence $R$ and $S$ are inverse exact category equivalences. This argument proves full faithfulness from the actual unit and counit. It does not deduce it from composition matrices. By induction transitivity, ordinary Levi Vermas go to ordinary $\mathfrak g$ Vermas; the corresponding column-generalized Vermas go to their genuine column-parabolic inductions. The Levi integrability criterion restricts the equivalence to the column-parabolic subcategories just as in step 7.1; projective covers again follow by exact equivalence. [F4, step 10.1, step 11.1, construct, algebra]

13.1 Each finite Levi factor block has a finite projective generator (finite label orbit and [F2], or its parabolic reflector). For two outer tensor projectives, their Hom is the tensor product of their factor Homs, by tensor-Hom and the finite-dimensional factor Hom spaces; applying a factor-projective Hom successively is exact: a fixed weight for the other factors cuts a finite-generated factor-$\mathcal O$ module, since PBW bounds the negative monomials in those fixed coordinates; factor projectivity therefore applies weight by weight. The resulting multiplicity module is in the remaining factor $\mathcal O$, by the same PBW finiteness with the finitely many generator weights of the projective. Their outer tensor sum therefore is projective, and its simple quotients cover all factor tuples. Those tuples exhaust the simple labels of the direct-sum Lie algebra: the outer tensor of the factor simples is cyclic on the tensor of their highest vectors. Any nonzero submodule has a highest vector by positive-root local finiteness and bounded highest-weight support; taking invariants successively in the separate positive root algebras leaves only that tensor highest line, because a simple highest-weight factor has no other highest vector. The submodule thus contains the cyclic generator, proving simplicity and identifying the unique simple quotient of the direct-sum Verma. Thus the outer tensor generator gives finite presentations of every object and has the tensor-product endomorphism algebra. Applying the generator Hom and its presentation inverse proves the product description in the Statement. This also proves standard/simple/projective tensor labels as objects, not just as classes. [F2, F4, step 12.1, construct, algebra]

14.1 The original tableau convention gives $\eta_i+\rho_i=a_i+(N-1)/2$, so dot sorting is literally stable sorting of the $a_i$. In the sorted $\kappa$ block the Levi coordinate is $a_t+B_\kappa+t-1$. The integral coordinate from the Statement is $a_t-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa+t-1$; their difference is exactly $\delta_\kappa$. Tensoring with the one-dimensional Lie algebra representation $x\mapsto\delta_\kappa\operatorname{tr}(x)$ is an exact inverse equivalence with inverse shift $-\delta_\kappa$, and its tensor associativity is ordinary scalar multiplication. It carries highest vectors, induced standards, simple heads and projective covers. Since a ground entry in global row $r$ is $c_\kappa+1-r$, its integral image is $1-(r-n+n_\kappa)$; these are the actual bottom-aligned integral ground rows. The retained heights give $m_j=q_j-n_\kappa$ nonincreasing and $m_j+1-(1-n_\kappa)=q_j$. For an admitted-ground label, subtracting its original ground entry gives a nonnegative integer; the displayed dictionary preserves that difference. Its integral entry is therefore at least the corresponding bottom-aligned integral ground entry and lies in the fixed admitted alphabet of [F4]. For an arbitrary genuine label the scalar shift still gives an integral parabolic highest weight, but no fixed-cut membership follows. Thus the height/charge dictionary holds generally and the fixed admitted component hypotheses of [F4] hold on the stated admitted-ground subcategories, without treating a nonintegral scalar trace character as an algebraic determinant character. [F4, step 7.1, step 13.1, construct, algebra]

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$, $R=S_{(0)}$, and $P_R=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed
antidominant projective. Write $\operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S^W$
for the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
$\sigma_\lambda(f)(\epsilon)=f(\lambda+\rho+\epsilon)$, and define
$$a_\lambda\colon Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}R\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R,\qquad z\otimes r\longmapsto\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))\otimes r.$$
Then $a_\lambda$ and the action map $Z\otimes R\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)$
are surjective and have the same kernel, inducing a canonical $R$-algebra
isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\cong R\otimes_{R^W}R.$$
On a generic Verma constituent of highest weight $x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon$, $z$
acts by the scalar
$\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(x(\lambda+\rho)+\epsilon)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))(x^{-1}\epsilon)$;
these scalars vary with $x$, and the center need not act by a single scalar on
$P_R$. After tensoring the right $R$ factor with the residue field at $0$, the
endomorphism algebra becomes $C=S/(S^W_+S)$. More generally, for dot-dominant
integral $\nu$ the corresponding algebra is $R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R$, where
$W_\nu$ is the dot stabilizer. Translation out of that facet identifies the
singular antidominant projective with the regular one; under these shifted
Harish-Chandra identifications, its induced endomorphism map is the inclusion
$R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R$.
facts: [F7] The deformed family $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]]; for every $x\in W$ the lift $P_R(x,\lambda)$ exists, is unique up to isomorphism, has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same multiplicities as its closed fiber, satisfies Hom base change for every map of deformation algebras, has finite free Hom modules into finite Verma-filtered targets, and a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map of such objects that is an isomorphism on the residue fiber is an isomorphism; for a dot-dominant integral target $\nu$ the same construction gives the lifts with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_\nu$ ([[thm-lifting-of-indecomposable-projectives-to-the-deformed-family]], [[prop-base-change-freeness-and-specialization-in-the-deformed-family]]).
uses: 1.4 Let $u=\nu+\rho$ be dominant with $H=\operatorname{Stab}(u)$, and $v=\lambda+\rho$ regular dominant. For onto translation, a retained factor satisfies $yv+\gamma=xu$. The norm bound and dominant-distance inequality force equality $|\gamma|=|u-v|$ and $x^{-1}yv\in Hv$; because $v$ is regular this means $x^{-1}y\in H$, hence $xu=yu$. Thus the retained standard is $\Delta(y\cdot\nu)$ once. This uses the coset condition, not the false assertion $Hv=\{v\}$. For return translation the retained labels are $x\in yH$, each extremal weight once. The conclusion is a Verma flag with factors $\Delta(yh\cdot\lambda)$ for $h\in H$, not a direct sum. The same calculation applies to the deformed tensor flags, with the common parameter $\tau$ retained. [F4, F6, F7, algebra]

3.1 Localize $P_R$ to $T=R_p$. Its full flag still has $|W|$ factors; CRT in the finitely many residual central characters splits it into pair components and singleton components. Write $P_{T,\{A,B\}}$ for one pair summand. Only this summand has the two factors $\Delta_T(A)$ and $\Delta_T(B)$ once. Maximal-weight generation gives $0\to\Delta_T(A)\to P_{T,\{A,B\}}\to\Delta_T(B)\to0$. It is projective in its character component by base change and splitting. The residual extension cannot split: otherwise its direct summand $M(B)$ would be projective, but duality applied to the nonsplit length-two $M(A)$ yields a nonsplit extension $0\to L(A)\to D M(A)\to L(B)=M(B)\to0$, contradicting projectivity. At a singleton the summand has a single standard. The identical argument applies to the singular once-each flag, with root-fixed labels giving singletons. Over the fraction field all standard characters are distinct and all Vermas are simple by the Shapovalov determinant; hence each component is its indicated standard and the generic endomorphism algebra is the tuple algebra. [F3, F5, F7, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Translation out carries $P_R^\nu$ to a regular projective by the exact tensor biadjunction and the actual central projectors. Its flag contains every regular standard once by steps 2.1 and 1.4. On the closed fiber, onto translation takes the regular antidominant simple Verma to the singular antidominant simple Verma, so adjunction gives a one-dimensional Hom from the return projective to the regular antidominant simple. Its regular antidominant cover splits off; both have every standard once, so the complement has zero flag and vanishes. Hom base change and the two-map lifting argument of [F7] now give $T_{\mathrm{out}}P_R^\nu\cong P_R^\lambda$. Any two choices induce the same endomorphism map after identification, since the endomorphism algebra is commutative (as will follow from its generic tuple embedding). [F6, F7, step 2.1, step 1.4, algebra]

5.1 The generic tuple embeddings place $\operatorname{End}(P_R)$ and $B$ (or $\operatorname{End}(P_R^\nu)$ and $B^H$) inside the same tuple algebra. Both are finite free right-$R$ modules: for End this is [F7], for $B^H$ it is Reynolds averaging in step 2.2. Steps 3.1, 2.2 and 4.1 identify their localizations at each height-one prime, pair by pair, including the singular singletons. A finite free $R$-lattice equals the intersection of its height-one localizations inside its fraction-field span. Indeed $R$ is a localization of a polynomial UFD, and $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}p=1}R_p$: a reduced fractional denominator outside $R$ has a nonunit irreducible factor detected at its prime; applying this coefficientwise to any free lattice basis proves the lattice assertion. Thus the two lattices are equal and yield the asserted algebra identification. This does not yet assert that the global central image is saturated; its surjectivity is established separately below. [F7, F8, step 2.2, step 4.1, algebra]

7.1 The image of $a_\lambda$ is an $R$-submodule of the finite free target $B$ respectively $B^H$ whose cokernel is finitely generated and has zero closed fiber by step 6.1; Nakayama over the local ring $R$ makes the cokernel zero, so $a_\lambda$ is surjective, and the action map $Z\otimes R\to\operatorname{End}(P_R)$ is surjective with it under the identification of step 5.1. [F7, step 5.1, step 6.1]

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). At $s=1$ the source Fock
pairing gives $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$ and
$\langle[P],[N]\rangle=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)$ for projectives $P$ and
finite-length $N$. Genuine generalized-standard/costandard Hom has its separate
delta pairing
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M(A),\nabla(B))=\delta_{AB}\mathbb C,$$
transported by restricted duality and the typed opposite filtered equivalence.

At general $s$ the source forms are $\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta$ and
$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta$; their labelled raw Gram matrix is
$B_\psi^{-1}$, not the identity. They satisfy
$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta$, $C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta$ and the
complementary duality. On the highest constituent let $C_0$ be the normalized
$\mathcal E\mathcal F$-swap bilinear form; for weight $\Lambda-\alpha$ the actual
library polarization is $s^{-a(\alpha)}C_0$ with
$a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$. Hence the library upper family uses its
own form-adjoint bar and the rescaling of
[[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; the two
source forms and the library form are not conflated.
facts: [F2] Parabolic Hom and duality ([[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]], [[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]): $\operatorname{Hom}(M(A),\nabla(B))=\delta_{AB}\mathbb C$ in each block, restricted duality, and BGG reciprocity.

[F3] Library polarization ([[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]], [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]): the normalized highest constituent form $C_0$, the weight recursion $a(\alpha)-a(\alpha-\alpha_i)=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+1$, and the library form $B_8$.
uses: 1.2 **The highest-constituent form $C_0$.** On irreducible highest constituents the normalized nondegenerate restriction of the reverse-factor bilinear form is $C_0$; the dictionary sends the library $\sigma$ with $\sigma(F_i)=t^{-1}K_iE_i$ to the source anti-involution acting by $sD^{-1}E$, which contributes $s^{-\langle\mu,h_i\rangle-1}$ on a target vector of weight $\mu$, and the exponent identity $a(\alpha)-a(\alpha-\alpha_i)=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+1$ with highest normalization and induction on lowering monomials proves $B_8=s^{-a}C_0$ on every weight space of the constituent. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 **The standard/costandard pairing.** The pairing $\operatorname{Hom}(M(A),\nabla(B))=\delta_{AB}\mathbb C$ is the actual generalized-standard Hom theorem of the block structure [F2], transported by restricted duality and the typed opposite filtered equivalence; it is not a restriction of the ordinary Verma lemma, and it is a separate pairing from the source Fock forms. The types original/reverse/dual and ordinary/adjoint bars remain explicit: the library upper family uses the form-adjoint bar and the rescaling of [F3], not the bare source forms. [F2, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1]

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the positive biadjoint
residue $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ action of
[[lem-residue-casimir-operators-give-local-affine-hecke-actions]].

At a coincident eigenvalue the completed degenerate affine Hecke algebra on $r$
steps is $\mathrm{Mat}_{r!}$ over the completed symmetric polynomial centre.
The first-$i$ image in its central fibre is $\mathrm{Mat}_{i!}(Z_{i,r})$, where
$$Z_{i,r}=\mathbb C[c_1,\dots,c_i]/(h_{r-i+1},\dots,h_r)$$
(with $c_j$ the elementary symmetric functions of $x_1,\dots,x_i$ and
$\sum_jh_jz^j=(1-c_1z+\cdots+(-1)^ic_iz^i)^{-1}$) is a finite local
complete-intersection Frobenius ring of dimension $\binom{r}{i}$ with
one-dimensional socle. Divided residue functors and the complementary-idempotent
restriction have the corresponding simple head and socle.

Consequently $e_iL(A)$ and $f_iL(A)$ are either $0$ or self-dual
indecomposables with simple isomorphic head and socle labelled
$\tilde e_iA$, respectively $\tilde f_iA$. Vanishing is exactly the absence of
the corresponding crystal edge. This retains the complete residue-translation
crystal claim, not only its $K_0$ action.
facts: [F1] Local affine-Hecke action ([[lem-residue-casimir-operators-give-local-affine-hecke-actions]]): the relations $T_j^2=1$, braid/distant commutation, commuting $x_j$, $T_jx_j-x_{j+1}T_j=-1$, local nilpotence of $x_j-i$, and biadjoint mates on the dual functors.

[F4] Fock and parabolic structure ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], [[thm-parabolic-kl-polynomials-give-the-dual-canonical-transition-matrix]]): the source upper chart, its two positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing, and the label dictionary $A\mapsto\tilde e_iA,\tilde f_iA$.
uses: 1.1 **Polynomial model and completion.** On $P_r=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ the operators $T_j=s_j-\partial_j$ with $\partial_j=(1-s_j)/(x_j-x_{j+1})$ satisfy the degenerate affine Hecke relations of [F1]; PBW spanning follows by ordered monomials and independence of the leading permutation operators after localizing away from the root differences. At the coincident eigenvalue, $x_i-x_{i+1}+1$ is a unit, so $\partial_i=(x_i-x_{i+1}+1)^{-1}(1-T_i)$ with the inverse on the left; hence the completed algebra is the polynomial/divided-difference endomorphism algebra $\mathrm{End}_{P_r^{S_r}}(P_r)$. [F1, algebra]

1.3 **The height filtration.** Fix one residue, write $E,F$ for its biadjoint functors and $e,f$ for their class operators, and put $h_+(b)=\max\{j:e^jb\ne0\}$, $h_-(b)=\max\{j:f^jb\ne0\}$ and $d(b)=h_+(b)+h_-(b)+1$ for a simple class $b$. These are finite by [F1]; at weight $\lambda$, ordinary $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ string theory gives $d(b)=2h_+(b)+\lambda+1=2h_-(b)-\lambda+1$. Positivity implies that every simple constituent $c$ of $eb$ has $h_+(c)\le h_+(b)-1$, so $d(c)\le d(b)$; the $f$ argument is identical. Hence the Serre subcategory generated by simples with $d\le r$ is stable under $E,F$. If $T$ is a simple subobject of $E^jM$, adjunction gives a nonzero map $F^jT\to M$; its image contains a simple subobject $S$ of $M$, and the preceding bound gives $d(S)\le d(T)$. The dual argument applies to simple quotients. Consequently translates of an object of height at most $r$ whose simple head and socle constituents all have height $r$ have the same property. [F1, algebra]

3.1 **An extremal simple.** Suppose $FS=0$ and put $n=h_+([S])$. Positivity and $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ string theory imply $[E^{(n)}S]=m[T]$ for a single simple $T$ and an integer $m>0$: the positive extremal classes give a bijection between the lowest and highest simple classes. Indeed $f^ne^n[S]=(n!)^2[S]$; each positive summand of $e^n[S]$ must return to a multiple of $[S]$, and $e^nf^n$ is the same nonzero scalar on the highest weight space, forcing all these summands to be the same simple class. Since $[F^{(n)}E^{(n)}S]=[S]$, integrality and positivity force $m=1$. Thus $E^{(n)}S$ is simple. The full Hecke multiplicity module in $E^nS\cong n!E^{(n)}S$ is the unique simple module $K_n$ of the central fibre, of dimension $n!$, by step 2.1. [F1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.3, algebra]

3.2 **Head, socle and the maximal-height constituent.** More generally suppose $E^{(n)}S$ is simple, where $n=h_+([S])$, and let $0\le j\le n$. The complement-idempotent restriction of $K_n$ in step 2.2 has simple head and socle over the remaining $(n-j)$-step algebra. Applying $E^{n-j}$ to $\operatorname{soc}E^{(j)}S$ embeds its image in that restriction tensored with the extremal simple. Step 1.3 ensures that each simple socle summand has height $d([S])$ and survives this translate. Two such summands, or two copies of one, would give a direct sum of two nonzero submodules inside a module with simple socle. Thus $E^{(j)}S$ has simple socle $T_j$; the opposite-category argument gives a simple head. Its socle multiplicity module in $E^jS\cong j!E^{(j)}S$ is $K_j$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,E^{(j)}S)$ along a composition series bounds the endomorphism dimension by the composition multiplicity of $T_j$, since Hom from a simple to this object is one-dimensional for $T_j$ and zero otherwise. This multiplicity is at most $\binom nj$, since $E^{(n-j)}E^{(j)}S\cong\binom nj E^{(n)}S$. On the other hand the Hecke action has dimension at least $(j!)^2\binom nj$: its kernel lies in the intersection of the first-$j$ algebra with the maximal central ideal of the full completed matrix algebra. Step 2.2 identifies the corresponding quotient as $\mathrm{Mat}_{j!}(Z_{j,n})$, of precisely that dimension. The two bounds force equality and show that $T_j$ occurs $\binom nj$ times and is the only constituent surviving $E^{n-j}$. The head has the same height and survives, so it is also $T_j$. All other constituents have strictly smaller height. [F1, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 1.3, algebra]

4.1 **A general simple.** Put $r=h_-([S])$ and choose a simple quotient $L$ of $F^{(r)}S$. Positivity implies $FL=0$, and adjunction embeds $S$ into $E^{(r)}L$. Step 3.1 makes $E^{(n+r)}L=T$ simple for $n=h_+([S])$. The divided-functor composition, obtained by the idempotent ranks of step 2.2, gives $E^{(n)}E^{(r)}L\cong\binom{n+r}{r}T$. Exactness therefore makes $E^{(n)}S$ a nonzero semisimple sum $mT$. Since $ET=0$, the $F$ version of step 3.2 applies to $T$ and gives $F^{(n)}T$ simple socle. Adjunction yields $m=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(E^{(n)}S,T)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}(S,F^{(n)}T)\le1$. Thus $E^{(n)}S$ is simple, and step 3.2 applies to every simple $S$. Interchanging $E,F$ gives both residue directions. A nonzero one-step translate has simple isomorphic head and socle and is indecomposable, since a nontrivial direct sum would have at least two simple head constituents. This proves the categorical conclusion before assigning tableau labels. [F1, step 2.2, step 3.1, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 **Self-duality and labels.** The residue functors commute with restricted duality and the input simple is self-dual, so its translates are self-dual; step 4.1 gives indecomposability and their simple isomorphic head and socle. The source-upper Chevalley leading-term argument of Kashiwara's string theory, with its balanced kernel and string decompositions checked against the two source-positive coefficient charts and the typed reverse pairing, gives $fG=[\varphi]G(\tilde f)$ and $eG=[\varepsilon]G(\tilde e)$ in each associated string, and comparing at $1$ with the categorical unique maximal-height factors of step 3.2 identifies the labels $\tilde e_iA$ and $\tilde f_iA$ of [F4]. [F1, F4, step 3.2, step 4.1]

This includes repeated-entry singular ambient characters. The proof uses

facts: [F3] Singular/parabolic coefficients ([[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]], [[thm-weyl-character-formula]]): the ordinary spherical values $P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)$ compute the singular multiplicities, and the finite Weyl character formula gives the signed Levi expansion of characters.

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the deformed family of
[[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] with $T$ a
localization of $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ and $M,N\in\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$:

1. The canonical map
$$U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_ZT\longrightarrow\bigl(\operatorname{End}_T(M_T(\lambda))\bigr)^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto\bigl(m\mapsto u\cdot m\cdot t\bigr),$$
is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras, the superscript denoting the $\mathfrak g$-finite part for the adjoint action $X\cdot f=X\circ f-f\circ X$, and the center $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ acting on $T$ through the shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ ([[thm-harish-chandra-isomorphism-for-the-center]]) followed by evaluation at $\lambda+\rho+\epsilon$ on the universal parameter $\epsilon$.
2. For finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules $E,F$, the $T$-module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$
is free of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^{*})_0$, and the natural base-change map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes\kappa(\epsilon)}(M\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon),N\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon))$$
is an isomorphism for every $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Spec}T$.
3. $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)$ is locally free of finite rank over $T$.
4. If a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism on the special fiber at $0$, it is an isomorphism.
facts: [F2] For every complex closed fiber of the polynomial family, the Duflo–Joseph theorem identifies $U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi$ with the $\mathfrak g$-finite endomorphisms of the corresponding Verma module and gives $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0$; over $Z$, the module $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is free of rank $\dim E_0$ ([[thm-duflo-joseph-g-finite-endomorphisms-of-verma-modules]], [[lem-kostant-adjoint-isotypic-multiplicities-have-zero-weight-rank]]).
uses: 2.1 Every complex point of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ gives kernel dimension $\dim G_0$ by [F2], so $A$ has the same rank $s$ at every such point. Every $(s+1)$-minor therefore vanishes as a polynomial; the $s$-minors generate the unit ideal, because otherwise a maximal ideal containing them would be an evaluation ideal by [[cor-weak-nullstellensatz-algebraically-closed-coordinate-form]], contradicting rank $s$ there. On an open where an $s$-minor is invertible, row and column elimination gives $\operatorname{diag}(I_s,0)$. Thus the kernel is finite projective of rank $\dim G_0$ and commutes with arbitrary base change. This argument is over $S$, so it applies to every localization $T$, even one whose closed points are not complex evaluation points. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For each finite-dimensional simple $L$, the adjoint $L$-multiplicity module of $U\otimes_ZS$ is $S\otimes_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(L,\mathcal H)$ by the harmonic decomposition [F3] and [F2]; it is finite free of rank $\dim L_0$. The action maps it to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(L,\operatorname{End}_S M_S(\lambda))$, which by tensor-Hom adjunction is the kernel from step 2.1 for $G=L^*$. At every complex point this map is an isomorphism by Duflo–Joseph [F2]. Its cokernel is finite and vanishes by local Nakayama at every maximal ideal of $S$; the resulting surjection splits onto the projective target, and its kernel, a projective module of rank zero, vanishes on each local free chart. Hence it is an isomorphism. Localizing gives the same result over $T$. Finite-dimensional complete reducibility decomposes every finite adjoint submodule, so these isotypic isomorphisms prove (1). [F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited through the Skryabin, natural
Whittaker and category-O projective/tilting suppliers. The finite Hecke
calculations below require only finite-dimensional linear algebra.

For $I=\mathbb Z$ (and reflected auxiliary finite cuts used to realize this
global statement), the map $t$ sends $\Lambda_i$ to $\Lambda_{-i}$ and
$\alpha_i$ to $\alpha_{-i}$, so $m^t=(-m_l,\dots,-m_1)$. The sign map
$\sigma(s_r)=-s_r$, $\sigma(x_r)=-x_r$ gives
$H^\Lambda_\alpha\cong H^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$ and intertwines residue $i$
with $-i$. Multipartition transpose with reversed components gives
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha\cong\mathrm{Col}^{\Lambda^t}_{\alpha^t}$, sending
$\mathrm{Rev}$ to target $\mathrm{Std}$. The genuine sourced Specht/sign
comparison is $\sigma^*S(A^t)\cong S(A)^{\circledast}$, and for
$A\in\mathrm{Rev}$ the simple and projective-cover labels are $A^t\mapsto A^\downarrow$;
no off-standard $D(A)$ is made into a simple. At parameter one these are maps on
the projected highest constituent/costandard and standard lattices, rather than
a naive permutation of all simple labels or all ambient monomial vectors.

For a finite bounded category-O chunk define $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)=\pi P_{\mathcal O}(A)$
for EVERY $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, and
$\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)=\pi T_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for EVERY
$A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$. The existing signed-Young comparison identifies
$\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ with $\sigma^*Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A^t)$; on
$\mathrm{Rev}$ it is the projective cover $Y(A^\downarrow)$. All these families
retain their ordinary self-dual source scope. Take FULL sums over
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$, with one representative each:
$\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}$ is the quasihereditary
Schur-cover algebra, and
$\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(\widetilde Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}$ is its
Ringel dual. Off-standard $Y_{\mathrm{all}}$ are indecomposable nonprojective
$H$-images, so summing only standard projective covers is not this full Young
generator. The Ringel category is the reversed-Levi/opposite-parabolic block,
using $F=D\Psi$ with its explicit shifts and
$F(\overline P(A))=T_{\mathcal O}(A)$; it is not an unqualified longest-Borel
twisting equivalence. For a proper original lower ideal the corresponding
opposite category is the matching highest-weight Serre quotient. Positive
finite multiplicities give Morita-equivalent generator algebras. The global
sign and these bounded-chunk categorical constructions have their stated
distinct domains.
facts: [F1] The Hecke simple and projective classes are indexed by $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, with standard-labelled classes $[D(A)]\mapsto D_A$ and $[Y(A)]\mapsto P_A$ ([[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]).

[F3] The actual finite-W tensor transport and regular-row corner are the natural identifications of [[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]], [[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]. The latter sends generalized standards to intrinsic Spechts and standard-labelled simples to simple heads. The tilting supplier proves the standard-socle criterion: every simple embedded in any generalized standard has standard label, and $P(B)=T(B^\uparrow)$ for standard $B$.
uses: 1.6 **The correctly normalized exterior quotient.** Choose a sufficiently low finite cut $k$, put $q_i=m_i+1-k$, $n=q_1$ and $c=n+k-1$. The ordinary parabolic ground has scalar $q_1+\cdots+q_{i-1}+m_i$, obtained from the head character $-\rho_i=\sum_{j\le i}q_j-n$ plus $c$. The finite-W tail shift is a different embedding convention and is not substituted for this character; the transported roots are nevertheless exactly $m_i=c+q_i-n$. For the transposed component partitions $\nu^{(i)}=(\lambda^{(i)})^{\mathsf T}$ form the exterior suffix module $D=\mathbb C_c\otimes\bigotimes_{i=l}^1\bigwedge^{\nu^{(i)}}(V/V_{i-1})$. Its tensor quotient $q:U=\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}\to D$ is parabolic-linear and hence finite-W-linear. Select $d$ distinct longest row names with idempotent $e_S$ and cyclic rightmost-row tensor $w$; regular evaluation identifies $H\to e_SU$, $b\mapsto wb$, with left corner action $a(wb)=w(ab)$. Therefore $K=\ker(q\,\mathrm{reg})$ is a LEFT ideal; no right-Hecke linearity of the exterior quotient is assumed. [F3, F4, construct, algebra]

2.1 **The Specht and reverse-standard simple comparisons.** The evaluation maps have $x_j=m+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$, so [F2] makes each evaluated Specht factor self-dual. Twisting its reflected evaluation by $\sigma$ changes $-m$ to $m$ and every Jucys transposition to its sign twist. Ordinary conjugate-Specht/sign duality, followed by the reversed-induction isomorphism of step 1.5, gives $\sigma^*S(A^t)=S(A)^\circledast$. For $A\in\mathrm{Rev}$ put $B=A^\downarrow$. The actual tilting bottom flag gives an embedding $M(A)\hookrightarrow T(A)=P(B)$, hence $S(A)\hookrightarrow Y(B)$ by exactness. The symmetric trace identifies a primitive projective cover $He$ with $(eH)^*$; since $Z\mapsto eZ$ is exact, this is the injective hull of its split simple top, with unique essential socle $D(B)$. Every nonzero submodule therefore contains that socle, giving $\operatorname{soc}S(A)=D(B)$: $S(A)$ is nonzero by its affine-PBW induced basis, and the socle of any nonzero submodule of this injective hull is its unique essential simple socle. Duality converts it to the simple head of $S(A)^\circledast$. Since $A^t$ is standard, the target standard-head statement and exact sign pullback now give $\sigma^*D(A^t)=D(A^\downarrow)$. No arbitrary quotient is assumed to preserve a head or socle. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.5, algebra]

2.2 **The full Young generator algebra.** For every $A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda$ put $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A):=\pi P_{\mathcal O}(A)$; by step 1.3 full faithfulness on projectives makes these nonzero indecomposable with local endomorphism rings, and makes them pairwise nonisomorphic, while for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ they are the projective covers $Y(A)$ of [F1]. If some $Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ were projective, it would be a sum of standard projective covers, and full faithfulness on the distinct O-projectives $P_{\mathcal O}(A)$ would give an identification of two nonisomorphic O-projectives, a contradiction; so off-standard images are nonprojective. Taking the full finite sum $Y_{\mathrm{all}}=\bigoplus_{A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda}Y_{\mathrm{all}}(A)$ (one representative each) and using full faithfulness on the corresponding full projective generator $Q=\bigoplus_AP_{\mathcal O}(A)$ gives $\operatorname{End}_{H^\Lambda}(Y_{\mathrm{all}})^{op}\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(Q)^{op}$, the quasihereditary Schur-cover algebra of [[thm-type-a-parabolic-category-o-ringel-duality-via-the-opposite-parabolic]] and [[def-the-ringel-dual-of-a-finite-highest-weight-ideal]]. Summing only the standard projective covers would give a Morita generator of $H^\Lambda$, which is symmetric and not quasihereditary in general, and is not the algebra meant here. [step 1.3, F1, given, algebra]

2.3 **An explicit trace-adjoint covector.** Positions have nonincreasing original column types $t_1\ge\cdots\ge t_d$, constant inside exterior blocks $J$. Put $p=\prod_j\prod_{i<t_j}(x_j-m_i)$, $a_-=\sum_{u\in J}\operatorname{sgn}(u)u$ and $g=pa_-=a_-p=g^*$. The native right dot formula on row tensors of columns $c_j$ is $vx_j=v_{L_j}+m_{c_j}v+\sum_{h<j,c_h\ge c_j}v(hj)-\sum_{h>j,c_h<c_j}v(jh)$. Let $\phi_0$ select the all-column-one tensor with fixed row order. Process the factors of $p$ in order $j=1,\ldots,d$, then $i=1,\ldots,t_j-1$. At that stage the target columns are $t_h$ for $h<j$, $i$ at $j$, and one for $h>j$. Transposing the dot formula has no earlier swap, since $t_h\ge t_j>i$, and no later swap, since $1\le i$; its diagonal is $m_i-m_i=0$. It therefore raises exactly that column by one with coefficient one. Thus $\phi_0R_p=\phi_{\mathbf t}$. The covector $\phi_{\mathbf t}R_{a_-}$ alternates inside each exterior block and vanishes on forbidden columns, so equals $\lambda q$ for an actual exterior covector $\lambda$. [F3, step 1.6, algebra]

3.1 **Descent to the projected lattices at parameter one.** At parameter one the simple classes are the projected vectors $D_A=\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A$ and the projective classes are $P_A=T_{A^\uparrow}$ by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; the sign and transpose maps of steps 1.1-1.2 act on these two families by the label rules $A\mapsto A^\downarrow$ for costandard vectors on $\mathrm{Rev}$ and by the inverse rectification for standard vectors, compatibly with the identification of [[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]]. This is the projected-lattice statement of the first paragraph; the map is not asserted to permute all monomials or all simple labels of the full Fock space, since the off-standard monomials have no simple image. [step 1.2, step 2.1, F1, given, algebra]

4.1 **Lifting the kernel in category $\mathcal O$.** Let $T=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathfrak g}(I^\Lambda\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ and $E(A)=\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathfrak p}^{\mathfrak g}(I^\Lambda\otimes D_0)$, with the ordinary ground $I^\Lambda$ and the exterior suffix factor $D_0$ above. Exact parabolic induction supplies $q:T\twoheadrightarrow E(A)$. Natural finite-W transport and regular evaluation identify $\pi(q)$ with the preceding exterior quotient and $\pi(R_g)$ with right multiplication by $g$. A finite total-column-degree filtration makes the nilradical act trivially on its graded finite Levi pieces; complete reducibility refines this to a standard flag of $E(A)$. The projective $T$ also has a standard flag. For any simple submodule $L$ of either standard-filtered object, choose the first flag term meeting $L$ nontrivially; simplicity gives containment there and zero intersection with the preceding term, hence an embedding of $L$ into that standard section. Its label is standard by [F3]. Every nonzero submodule has a simple socle because this is a finite-length chunk, so exactness and the nonzero standard-simple image make $\pi$ detect nonzero SUBMODULES of these two objects. This does not assert conservativity on the whole category. Since $\pi(R_g\ker q)=0$, detection gives $R_g\ker q=0$. Thus $R_g$ factors as $Fq$ with $F:E(A)\to T$. Its Schur image is the injective map $H/K\to Hg\subset H$; detection on submodules of $E(A)$ makes $F$ injective. Hence $\ker q=\ker R_g$ as actual category-$\mathcal O$ submodules. [F3, F4, A1, step 3.3, construct, algebra]

5.1 **A genuine tilting module, not just its character.** The self-dual prinjective ground carries a perfect restricted contravariant form, and its tensor product with the natural tensor dot product gives a symmetric nondegenerate contravariant form $B_T$; Casimir and place permutations are self-adjoint, hence so is $g$. The form $B_E(qt,qu)=B_T(t,R_gu)$ is well defined by the actual kernel equality of step 4.1. If $qt$ is in its radical, self-adjointness and nondegeneracy of $B_T$ force $R_gt=0$, hence $qt=0$. It is symmetric and contravariant, and finite weight spaces make it a perfect restricted form. Thus $E(A)$ is self-dual. Dualizing its already established standard flag gives a costandard flag, so it is a tilting object; arbitrary parabolic induction has not been asserted to preserve tiltings. [F3, F4, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 **The leading tilting summand.** For a product of wedges with lengths $\nu_s$, occupation of the first $r$ coordinates is at most $\sum_s\min(r,\nu_s)=\sum_{a\le r}\lambda_a$. Equality at the highest weight forces every wedge of length at least $a$ to contain its $a$th initial coordinate; that tensor is unique. In a suffix allocation, slots can move only to later Levi blocks. If $u_{<j}$ slots originally before $j$ move to block $j$ or later, the degree before $j$ drops by $u_{<j}$, while at most $u_{<j}$ moved slots can increase the first $r$ coordinates in block $j$. Thus every resulting highest partition $\beta$ satisfies $\sum_{i<j}|\beta^{(i)}|+\sum_{a\le r}\beta_a^{(j)}\le\sum_{i<j}|\lambda^{(i)}|+\sum_{a\le r}\lambda_a^{(j)}$. Any moved slot gives a strict component boundary; equality everywhere forces the unique original leading tensor. Exact induction consequently gives $[E(A):M(A)]=1$ with all other standards strictly lower in multipartition dominance. [F3, F4, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Tilting classification and its leading-standard triangularity then yield $E(A)=T(A)\oplus\bigoplus_{\lambda(B)<\lambda(A)}T(B)^{\oplus m_B}$. This is an actual tilting decomposition obtained after step 5.1, not a module isomorphism inferred from characters alone. [F3, F4, step 5.1, algebra]

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda,\mu$ be dominant regular integral
weights for the same complex type-$A$ semisimple Lie algebra and fixed positive
system. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant member of $W(\mu-\lambda)$ and
$E=L(\nu)$ the finite-dimensional simple. The actual translation functors
$$F=T_\lambda^\mu=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}(E\otimes-)\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda},\qquad G=T_\mu^\lambda=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E^*\otimes-)\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\mu}$$
are exact mutually inverse equivalences, with natural adjunction isomorphisms
$\operatorname{Id}\cong GF$ and $FG\cong\operatorname{Id}$. They preserve the
dot-orbit labels: for every $w\in W$,
$$F\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu),\quad FL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu),\quad FP(w\cdot\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\mu),$$
and conversely for $G$. Consequently the two blocks have identical Verma-flag
and composition multiplicities, both equal to $P_{y,w}(1)$, and $F$ transports
the inverse-Kazhdan–Lusztig character identity as a Grothendieck-group identity
with the same signed weighted-inverse coefficients $q'_{w,x}(1)$ and the same
support $x\ge w$. Formal characters in the two blocks use their respective
weights $x\cdot\lambda$ and $x\cdot\mu$; they need not be equal as weight
series. The dominant/antidominant, Bruhat, left/right and inverse-Soergel-label
conventions are preserved. This is an ungraded categorical transport and
supplies no Ext or Koszul grading.
facts: [F11] Block conventions and multiplicities ([[def-regular-integral-dot-orbit-labelling-convention]], [[thm-projective-verma-multiplicities-are-kazhdan-lusztig-values-at-one]], [[thm-simple-verma-composition-multiplicities-are-kazhdan-lusztig-values]], [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]): in each of the regular integral blocks $\mathcal O_\lambda$, $\mathcal O_\mu$ the standards, simples and indecomposable projectives are labelled by $W$, the dominant label is $e$, the antidominant one $w_0$, $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ by BGG reciprocity, and both multiplicities equal $P_{y,w}(1)$, vanishing unless $y\le w$.

[F12] The inverse-Kazhdan–Lusztig character formula ([[thm-the-kazhdan-lusztig-character-formula-in-regular-integral-category-o]]): in $\mathcal O_\lambda$, $[L(w\cdot\lambda)]=\sum_xq'_{w,x}(1)[M(x\cdot\lambda)]$ with $q'_{x,w}$ the inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficients, supported on $x\ge w$.
uses: 6.1 Being inverse equivalences, $F$ is exact and reflects the categorical structures. For the labels: $F\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ was proved in step 2.1. For each $w$, $FL(w\cdot\lambda)$ is a simple object, and the exact functor $F$ turns the epimorphism $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow L(w\cdot\lambda)$ onto its unique simple quotient into an epimorphism $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)\cong F\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\twoheadrightarrow FL(w\cdot\lambda)$; since the simple quotient of $\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ is unique and equal to $L(w\cdot\mu)$, one has $FL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu)$. Finally $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ is a projective cover of $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ by [F8] and [F11], so $FP(w\cdot\lambda)$ is a projective object mapping onto $FL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu)$ with essential kernel: if a subobject $Z'\subseteq FP(w\cdot\lambda)$ mapped onto $FL(w\cdot\lambda)$, then applying the inverse equivalence would exhibit a subobject of $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ mapping onto $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, so essentiality on the source forces $Z'=FP(w\cdot\lambda)$. By uniqueness of projective covers in [F8], $FP(w\cdot\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\mu)$. The dual statements $G\Delta(w\cdot\mu)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$, $GL(w\cdot\mu)\cong L(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $GP(w\cdot\mu)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)$ follow from step 2.2 and the identical argument with the roles exchanged. [F8, F11, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 5.1]

7.1 The multiplicities are transported termwise. Since $F$ is an equivalence, it is full and faithful, so applying $F$ to a finite Verma flag of $P$ and applying $G$ to a finite Verma flag of $FP$ are inverse bijections between the flag multiplicities of $P$ and of $FP$; by steps 6.1 and 2.2 the labels match, giving $(FP(w\cdot\lambda):F\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ and, with step 6.1, $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=P_{y,w}(1)$ by [F11]; BGG reciprocity [F11] likewise transports the composition multiplicities and their vanishing. Transporting the identity of [F12] along the induced isomorphism of Grothendieck groups gives $[L(w\cdot\mu)]=\sum_xq'_{w,x}(1)[M(x\cdot\mu)]$ with the same weighted-inverse coefficients and the same support $x\ge w$, because $F$ carries $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ to $L(w\cdot\mu)$ and $M(x\cdot\lambda)=\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ to $M(x\cdot\mu)$. The conventions are preserved because the label $w$ is unchanged: dominant and antidominant labels, Bruhat comparisons, left/right labels and inverse Soergel labels carry over; the formal characters are read in the respective weight series $x\cdot\lambda$ and $x\cdot\mu$ and need not coincide. Nothing above uses or produces a grading on $\mathcal O$, an $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebra or a Koszul structure. [F11, F12, step 2.2, step 6.1] ∎

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a projective $P$ in a regular integral type-A
block, choose its polynomial Soergel lift $\mathsf B(P)$ determined by the
preceding projective dictionary: if $P=\bigoplus_wP(w\cdot\lambda)^{m_w}$, take
$\mathsf B(P)=\bigoplus_wB_{w^{-1}}^{m_w}$, so that its right reduction is
$V(P)$ after forgetting auxiliary grading. Write $r_{x,d}(\mathsf B(P))$ for
the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph module supported at
$x$ in its standard support filtration, with the standard-generator

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra and let $\mu$ be a highest weight. The action of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ on the Verma module $M(\mu)$ induces an algebra isomorphism
$$U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \bigl(\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)\bigr)^{\operatorname{ad}\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},$$
where the target is the locally finite part of the endomorphism algebra for
the adjoint action $x\mapsto[x,-]$. In particular
$\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Moreover, for every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $E$,
$$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0,$$
and the action identifies each finite adjoint isotypic multiplicity with that
dimension.
facts: [F6] The adjoint isotypic multiplicity lemma: $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U(\mathfrak g))$ is free over $Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ of rank $\dim E_0$, and $U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi$ has associated graded $A=S(\mathfrak g)/(p_1,\dots,p_r)$ for every central character, a reduced integral domain with Hilbert series $\prod_i(1-t^{d_i})/(1-t)^{2N+r}$ and $2N=\dim\mathfrak g-r$ ([[lem-kostant-adjoint-isotypic-multiplicities-have-zero-weight-rank]], [[lem-the-nilpotent-central-fiber-is-a-reduced-integral-domain]]).
uses: 3.1 Combining steps 1.5, 2.1 and 2.2, $$\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0$$ for every highest weight $\mu$ and every finite-dimensional $E$; the same computation with $E$ replaced by its dual identifies the adjoint isotypic multiplicity in $U(\mathfrak g)$-modules with $\dim E_0$, by the freeness statement of [F6]. [F6, step 1.5, step 2.1, step 2.2]

3.2 Suppose the action had nonzero kernel $K$ in $U_\chi=U(\mathfrak g)/U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$. Then the associated graded $\operatorname{gr}(K)$ is a nonzero graded ideal of the domain $A$ of [F6], so it contains $Af$ for a nonzero homogeneous $f$; multiplication by $f$ is injective and the complete-intersection Hilbert series of $A$ gives $\dim(A/Af)_{\le n}=O(n^{2N-1})$. Consequently the image of $U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)$ in $U_\chi$ has cumulative growth $O(n^{2N-1})$, contradicting the lower bound of step 2.3. Hence the action $U_\chi\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)$ is injective. [F6, step 2.3]

4.1 Surjectivity onto the locally finite part: the map of step 3.2 is $\mathfrak g$-equivariant for the adjoint actions, so it maps the $E$-isotypic component to the $E$-isotypic component for every finite-dimensional simple $E$. The source $E$-isotypic multiplicity is $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,U_\chi)=\dim E_0$ by [F6], and the target multiplicity is $\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E,\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(E\otimes M(\mu),M(\mu))=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M(\mu),E^{*}\otimes M(\mu))=\dim E_0$ by step 3.1. An injective linear map between spaces of equal finite dimension is an isomorphism, so the action is an isomorphism onto each isotypic component, hence onto the locally finite part. [F6, step 3.1, step 3.2]

5.1 Since the kernel of $U(\mathfrak g)\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}M(\mu)$ is exactly $\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)$ and the image of $U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$ lies in that kernel, steps 3.2 and 4.1 give both the algebra isomorphism and $\operatorname{Ann}M(\mu)=U(\mathfrak g)\ker\chi_\mu$; the multiplicity statement is step 3.1 read through the isomorphism. The Axiom of Choice is inherited from the published category-$\mathcal O$ and invariant-theory suppliers. [F6, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex
semisimple, $\lambda$ the dominant regular integral representative of a block
and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$.
Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan
reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then:

(1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
shifted by $\lambda+\rho$ in the published $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ convention,
followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
(multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel;

(2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$
identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective,
canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its
isomorphism class;

(3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the
coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or
used.

This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral
case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the
invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.

u$, $R^{W_
u}\otimes_{R^W}R$ specializes to $C^{W_
u}$.

[F1]

1.2 Specializing the right factor along $R\to\mathbb C$ (the residue field at $0$) carries algebra isomorphisms to algebra isomorphisms, and [F2] identifies $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\otimes_R\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(P_R\otimes_R\mathbb C)=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$, while the target specializes to $(R\otimes_{R^W}R)\otimes_R\mathbb C\cong R/(S\,S^W_+)=C$, and $a_\lambda$ specializes to the map sending $z$ to the class of $\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(\lambda+\rho+\tau)$. claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, a degree $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space with its finite W-algebra image
$W_d$ and cyclotomic Hecke image $B_d$. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$; this is the raw double centralizer.
2. For admissible origins, $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence between
   $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.
3. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact
   Schur Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples; it is fully
   faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all
   tiltings, and its left adjoint is right exact and recovers
   $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective.
4. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the algebra $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic
   algebra $H_d(\mathbf a)$; outside the stable range and for admissible
   origins the central-corner identification $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ is used.

Mutual centralizers alone do not give the Morita statement: the nonadmissible
origin example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$ and $d=2$ has a nonprojective tensor
module while the mutual centralizer identities still hold.
facts: [F1] The raw filtered double centralizer holds for every complex origin; for admissible origins the tensor space is a progenerator and $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence $W_d\text{-mod}\to B_d\text{-mod}$; the nonadmissible counterexample with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ separates the two assertions ([[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]]).

[F2] $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d$ and, componentwise, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha$ for admissible origins; the map $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ is surjective with injectivity exactly in the nonempty stable range and also in the trivial empty branch ([[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]]).

[F3] The Whittaker quotient $\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ is exact, its kernel is the Serre subcategory of off-standard simples, it is fully faithful on all projectives and on tiltings, its left adjoint $\pi^*=T\otimes_{B_d}-$ is right exact, and $\pi^*\pi$ recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective of the ambient category ([[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]).

[F4] The stable range is $q_l\ge d$; in it $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$, and outside it the admissible-origin image is the central block corner $fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ ([[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).
uses: 1.1 The raw double centralizer. For arbitrary complex origin the filtered leading-symbol lifting argument of [F1] gives $W_d=B_d'$ and $B_d=W_d'$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, with associated graded images the Vust centralizers; this is the all-origin clause and does not use admissibility. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Admissible Morita equivalence. Assume $c$ admissible. By the progenerator clause of [F1], $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator for $W_d$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence; by the component clause of [F2] its endomorphism algebra is $B_d=\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the equivalence is the standard one attached to the $(W_d,B_d)$-bimodule $V_c^{\otimes d}$, identifying $W_d$-mod with $B_d$-mod. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The Schur Serre quotient. The composite of the genuine Whittaker functor with the equivalence of step 1.2 is $\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ by [F2] and [F3]; it is exact and its kernel is the Serre subcategory generated by the off-standard simples, so it is the exact Schur Serre quotient killing exactly those simples. [F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Full faithfulness and the left adjoint. By [F3] the quotient is fully faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all tiltings, while its left adjoint $T\otimes_{B_d}-$ is only right exact and $\pi^*\pi$ recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective; these boundaries are part of the statement and are not repaired by changing conventions. [F3, step 2.1, given]

4.1 Stable range and central corner. For the empty pyramid degree zero is the scalar identity and positive degree is the zero-algebra identity, so all comparisons hold directly with $f=1$ in degree zero and $f=0$ in positive degree. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$ then $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ by [F4] and the component form of step 2.1 uses the full cyclotomic algebra; outside the stable range, and for admissible origins, the image is the central block corner $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ of [F4], with the component corners $B_\alpha=f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha$ of [F2]. For nonadmissible origins only the raw mutual centralizer statement of step 1.1 remains. [F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c$ be an admissible origin, let $P_c$ be the ground
simple projective-injective of the relevant summand of the parabolic category
$\mathcal O$ of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and let $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ with $V=\mathbb C^N$. Write
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ for the image of the right cyclotomic Hecke action of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] and $B_\alpha$ for its central
components. Then the right Hecke action gives an algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d,$$
and on each central component, cut by the central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of
$B_d$ acting on $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$,
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha =f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha,$$
where $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$ is the corresponding block of the cyclotomic Hecke
algebra. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the image is the full cyclotomic
algebra, $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ and $B_\alpha=H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$; a single
component is not identified with the entire degree-$d$ algebra. Outside the
stable range the central-corner identification uses the admissible-origin
corner of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The maps $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ are surjective in all cases,
and the full action $H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ is
injective precisely when $q_l\ge d$ for a nonempty pyramid. For the empty pyramid $l=N=0$, the degree-zero objects and algebras are $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$, and for $d>0$ they are $T_d=U_d=H_d=0$. All endomorphism identities hold there, and the raw action is faithful in every degree, including the zero-algebra action; $q_l$ is not defined in this branch.
facts: [F1] The right Hecke action on $T$ exists and its generators $x_j,s_i$ are natural endomorphisms of the tensor functor, commuting with $\mathfrak g$; the image is $B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$, and the Whittaker functor sends $T$ to $V_c^{\otimes d}$ ([[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]], [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]], [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]]).

[F2] The Whittaker functor is exact on $\mathcal O_c^d$, its kernel is the Serre subcategory generated by the off-standard simples, $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detector whose simple socle constituents are standard-labelled and whose indecomposable summands are precisely the standard-labelled projective-injective covers, each occurring with positive multiplicity, and $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$ ([[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]]).

[F3] The filtered double centralizer identifies the two image algebras on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ for every complex origin: $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers, and in particular $\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d$; for a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$ the full action of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful ([[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]]).

[F4] Outside the stable range the image of the Hecke action is a central block corner $fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ for admissible origins, and in the stable range $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ ([[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]).
uses: 1.1 The Hecke action lies in the g-endomorphisms. For the empty pyramid, the empty tensor in degree zero and its ground object give $T_0=U_0=H_0=\mathbb C$. In positive degree $V=0$ gives $T_d=U_d=0$, and the level-zero cyclotomic relation is the empty product $1$, so $H_d=0$. The stated endomorphism identities and faithfulness follow directly, with the unique zero-algebra map injective; the remaining argument assumes a nonempty pyramid. Each generator $x_j$ of the truncated tensor action is built from the trace Casimir and place permutations and commutes with the diagonal $\mathfrak g$-action; the place permutations are natural in the module variable, so the resulting right $H_d(\mathbf a)$-action on $T$ consists of $\mathfrak g$-endomorphisms, and its image is $B_d$ by definition. Hence there is a surjection $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ and an inclusion $B_d\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with the opposite convention fixed by the right action. [F1, algebra]

1.2 The Whittaker comparison is injective. Let $\varphi:T\to T$ be nonzero and put $X=\operatorname{im}\varphi$, a nonzero submodule of the finite-length object $T$. Choose a simple submodule $L(A)\subseteq X$; because $\operatorname{soc}X\subseteq\operatorname{soc}T$, [F2] gives $A\in\mathrm{Std}$. Exactness gives an injection $V(L(A))\hookrightarrow V(X)$, and the first module is nonzero, so $V(X)\ne0$. Exactness also identifies $V(X)$ with the image of $V(\varphi)$, hence $V(\varphi)\ne0$. This proves injectivity of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$. No restriction on all composition factors of $T$ is used. [F2, algebra]

2.1 The image of the comparison. On $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$ the induced map lands in the centralizer of the finite-W action, $\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$; by the filtered double centralizer [F3] this centralizer equals $B_d$; and the induced map contains $B_d$ because every Hecke generator on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ arises from the corresponding endomorphism of $T$ by [F1]. Since $B_d$ is the whole target, the injective map of step 1.2 is also surjective, so $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d$. [F1, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 Stable range. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$ then the action of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful by [F3] and the image is the full algebra $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$; a single central component is correspondingly a block $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$, not the whole algebra. Outside the stable range the corner identification of [F4] applies for admissible origins, while the map $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ remains surjective by step 1.1. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Central components. The central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of the finite-dimensional algebra $B_d$ decompose $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$ and $B_d=\bigoplus_\alpha B_\alpha$; applying the isomorphism of step 2.1 componentwise gives $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=f_\alpha B_df_\alpha=B_\alpha$. The component $B_\alpha$ sits inside the cyclotomic block as the corner $f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha$ by [F4]; it is not the entire degree-$d$ algebra. [F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Failure of raw faithfulness below the stable range. For a nonempty pyramid, suppose $d>q_l$ and use an enlargement by full ground rows with smallest height at least $d$. In its last column, raise the first $q_l+1$ entries above their ground values by $1$; raise its top entry further by $d-q_l-1$, and leave every other entry ground. This is column strict, has total degree $d$, and is standard: for columns with the same charge, the changed rightmost entry is at least every unchanged entry to its left in that row; different charge cosets are incomparable. The first $q_l$ rows of this column are retained, but its next row is deleted, so this standard label is noncontractible. Its nonzero large finite-W simple belongs to a complementary central block. Hence the supporting idempotent $f$ of [F4] is proper; the faithful large tensor progenerator makes $1-f$ nonzero also in the large Hecke algebra. The small raw action has the nonzero kernel $(1-f)H_d(\mathbf a)$ and is not faithful. Together with step 2.2 this proves the asserted precise stable-range criterion. [F2, F4, step 2.2, construct, algebra] ∎

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral block with dominant
representative $\lambda$:

1. Projective functors form a Krull-Schmidt category.
2. Their indecomposables are indexed by $W$, with $\Theta_w$ characterized by
$\Theta_w\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)$. For a reduced word
$w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the functor $\Theta_w$ is a multiplicity-one summand of
$\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, and every other indecomposable summand has a
label $x<w$. In particular every indecomposable projective functor is generated
as a summand by wall crossings.

claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.

For this embedding argument, enlarge a finite upper alphabet if necessary while keeping the lower endpoint and the Levi column heights fixed. The blocks of the original labels are unchanged, because their entry multisets are unchanged; the established Fock projection and its off-standard kernel apply on the enlarged alphabet, where the standard predicate for those labels is the same. Every generalized standard $M(B)$ then embeds into an iterated $e$-word applied to an irreducible standard $M(C)$: add successively huge offsets to the later columns so that all later entries lie above the earlier ones, making $C$ the unique minimum in its fixed-multiset tableau order and hence $M(C)=L(C)$ simple; then lower the later-column entries back, column by column and bottom to top, with the explicit residue word. A later column stays above the active residues, so a wrong move can only occur in an earlier column and strictly increases an earlier prefix weight; hence $B$ is the unique maximal final standard section and occurs once, and the canonical maximal trace embeds $M(B)$ at the bottom. If $L(A)$ embedded into $M(B)$ with $A$ off standard, adjunction would give the standard $L(C)$ as a quotient of an $f$-word applied to $L(A)$, impossible by kernel stability. [F4, step 3.1]
