claim:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a dominant regular
integral weight $\lambda$ of the complex type-$A$ Lie algebra and the standard
parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$, with reductive Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and longest
Levi Weyl element $w_J$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]). The
$\mathfrak p_J$-dominant weights in this regular block are exactly
$y\cdot\lambda$ for $y\in{}^JW$. Write
$\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=M_{\mathfrak p}(y\cdot\lambda)$,
$L(x\cdot\lambda)$ and $P^J(x\cdot\lambda)$ for its generalized standards,
simples and projective covers
([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]). Then for
$x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=(P^J(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)=n_{y,x}(1).$$

These are the antispherical sign coefficients, with support $y\le x$ and
diagonal $1$. The precise character/Grothendieck identity supplying the
formula is
$$\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}\operatorname{ch}\Delta(uy\cdot\lambda).$$

For the same highest weights in the antidominant base
$\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, the actual longest-left label is
$z=yw_0$, since $y\cdot\lambda=z\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$.
Its shortest-left encoding is $a=\mathrm{lf}(y):=w_Jyw_0\in{}^JW$, so the
weight in that encoding is $(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$, not
$a\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. With $b=\mathrm{lf}(x)$, the reindexed matrix is
$$\widetilde N_{a,b}:=n_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}(1)=n_{w_Jaw_0,\,w_Jbw_0}(1).$$
It is the same multiplicity matrix with both indices permuted and has reversed
support in the transported order. It is not in general $n_{a,b}(1)$.
Every label retains its explicit dot-baseweight.
The highest-weight category theorem applies also to singular integral
parabolic blocks, but this ordinary regular KL matrix formula assumes the
ambient central character is regular. No singular/parabolic category
equivalence, grading or Koszul duality is asserted.
facts: [F4] Ordinary regular multiplicities: for a dominant regular integral base, $[M(z\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=P_{z,x}(1)$ with vanishing unless $z\le x$ ([[thm-simple-verma-composition-multiplicities-are-kazhdan-lusztig-values]], [[def-regular-integral-dot-orbit-labelling-convention]]), and the alternating sum identity $n_{y,x}(1)=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)$ ([[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]] (1) at $v=1$); the labelling dictionary $W^J=({}^JW)^{-1}$ and the coset minima are [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]], [[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]].

[F5] The regular-to-regular translations of [[prop-translation-identifies-regular-integral-blocks]] identify labelled ordinary standards, simples and projective covers between dominant regular integral blocks of the same type-$A$ root datum, so [F4] holds in every such block, not only the principal one.
uses: 1.2 **The dominant labels.** Put $A=\lambda+\rho$, strictly dominant and integral. The weight $y\cdot\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p_J$-dominant iff $\langle yA,\alpha_j^\vee\rangle-1\ge0$ for every $j\in J$. The integer $\langle A,y^{-1}\alpha_j^\vee\rangle$ is positive exactly when $y^{-1}\alpha_j$ is a positive root: strict dominance makes positive-root coroot pairings positive integers and negative-root pairings negative. Thus the condition is $y^{-1}\alpha_j>0$ for all $j\in J$, equivalently no LEFT descent $s_jy<y$: in type $A$, $y^{-1}\alpha_j>0$ means that the position of value $j$ precedes that of $j+1$, exactly the inversion-length ascent condition for swapping those values. These are precisely the shortest-left representatives ${}^JW$ in the coset-minimum convention of [F4]; no inversion of the weight label is performed. [F4, algebra]

2.1 **Comparing simple coefficients.** By [F1] the parabolic simples are the $L(x\cdot\lambda)$, $x\in{}^JW$. Taking the coefficient of $L(x\cdot\lambda)$ in the identity of step 1.1 (with $\xi=y\cdot\lambda$, $y\in{}^JW$) and using [F4] and [F5] for the ordinary Vermas in the given dominant regular integral block gives $[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}[M(uy\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)=n_{y,x}(1)$. The sum is finite and the coefficients with $uy\not\le x$ vanish; in particular the support is $y\le x$ with diagonal $n_{x,x}(1)=1$. [F1, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.2 **Native longest-left labels.** Let $\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$. Dot-action composition gives $y\cdot\lambda=(yw_0)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$ and $x\cdot\lambda=(xw_0)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. If $y$ has no left descent in $J$, each $y^{-1}\alpha_j$ is positive, so $(yw_0)^{-1}\alpha_j=w_0y^{-1}\alpha_j$ is negative; hence $z=yw_0$ is the longest representative in its left $W_J$-coset. Its shortest-left encoding is $a=w_Jz=w_Jyw_0$, with inverse $y=w_Jaw_0$; similarly $b=w_Jxw_0$ has inverse $x=w_Jbw_0$. Consequently the same multiplicity of step 2.1 is $[\Delta^J((w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}):L((w_Jb)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}})]=n_{w_Jaw_0,w_Jbw_0}(1)=\widetilde N_{a,b}$. This is an honest permutation of rows and columns, with support transported from $w_Jaw_0\le w_Jbw_0$, not a claim that $\widetilde N_{a,b}=n_{a,b}(1)$. Choosing the transported reversed order reads the same matrix as lower triangular. [F1, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The preceding steps prove the multiplicity formula, its projective form, the character identity and the reindexed version; the statement that only the regular ambient central character is assumed, and that no singular/parabolic equivalence or grading is used, is exactly the scope of the quoted suppliers [F1]--[F5]. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

claim:

integral conventions of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]]. Put
$N=(n_{y,x}(1))_{y,x\in{}^JW}$, with rows indexed by generalized standards and

([[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]). Then $N$ is upper
unitriangular and, for each $x$,
$$\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{y\ge x}(N^{-1})_{x,y}\,\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda).$$

products of $n_{a,b}(1)$; they are weighted incidence inverses, not generally
ordinary Bruhat Mobius values. In the antidominant base $\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, set
$a=\mathrm{lf}(y)=w_Jyw_0$ and encode the same weight as
$(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. The reindexed matrix is
$\widetilde N_{a,b}=N_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}$
and its inverse is reindexed by the same permutation; thus the same formula
has reversed support in the transported order. This does not replace the
entries by $n_{a,b}(1)$.

character formula for the regular parabolic block, and constructs no Koszul or

The vectors $v_Sx_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$, $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$, have distinct leading tensors: the leading dot moves its box one column left, while a permutation changes the ordered distinct rows. Consequently $h:H_d(\mathbf a)\to e_SAe_S$, characterized by $h(b)v_S=v_Sb$, is an algebra isomorphism, and $\theta\mapsto\theta(v_S)$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A}(U,M)$ with $e_SM$ for every finite-image module $M$. The actual dot formula gives $v_Sx_A=v_{\mathbf j}$, where $\mathbf j$ has the ordered rows of $v_S$ and column sequence prescribed by $A-A_c$; subtracting $a_j$ cancels the scalar at column $j$ and moves that box one column left. A tilting has standard socle from its standard flag and standard head from its costandard flag and simple-preserving restricted duality. Any map from it to the off-standard cokernel vanishes, since a nonzero quotient would have standard head. claim:

algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by
[[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]],

$$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$
is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory
of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of

objects killed by $V$.
facts: [F1] The central action identifies $\operatorname{End}(P)$ with the local coinvariant algebra $C$, with maximal ideal $C_+$ and residue field $\mathbb C$ ([[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]], [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]). The top multiplication pairing is perfect and the socle of $C$ is one-dimensional ([[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]]).

uses: 1.1 An indecomposable injective has simple socle: embed its finite-length socle into the direct sum of the injective hulls from [F3], extend that embedding to the whole object by injectivity of the target, and note that the kernel is zero because any nonzero finite-length submodule meets the socle. Injectivity of the source splits the embedding; indecomposability and uniqueness of injective hulls then give one hull. Every simple submodule of a Verma-filtered object embeds into some flag factor (take the first flag position it meets), so [F2] forces its label to be $a$. Hence every projective-injective indecomposable is the injective hull of $L(a)$, and is isomorphic to $P$. In particular the socle of $P$ is $L(a)$, once. [F2, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 For a finite $C$-module $N$, define $L(N)=P\otimes_CN$ by a finite presentation: the cokernel of the corresponding map between finite sums of $P$ exists in $\mathcal O$. Tensor-Hom adjunction gives $L\dashv V$; exactness of $V$ and $VP=C$ give $VL(N)\cong N$ by applying $V$ to that presentation. The counit $LVM\to M$ becomes an isomorphism under $V$, so its kernel and cokernel lie in $\ker V$. This supplies the equivalence $\mathcal O_\lambda/\ker V\simeq C\text{-mod}$: in the quotient every object is isomorphic to one of the $L(N)$, and adjunction identifies their quotient Hom maps with module maps. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Choose a linear functional $\omega:C\to\mathbb C$ nonzero on the top degree and zero on the other degrees. By [F1], $c\mapsto(d\mapsto\omega(cd))$ identifies $C$ with its vector-space dual as a $C$-module. For a finite $C$-module $N$, $\operatorname{Hom}_C(N,C^*)\cong N^*$ by evaluation at $1$, with inverse $\ell\mapsto(n\mapsto[c\mapsto\ell(cn)])$. Thus $C$ is injective among finite $C$-modules. The two contravariant functors $\operatorname{Hom}(-,P)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_C(V-,C)$ are exact. Their canonical comparison is an isomorphism on simples by step 1.1 and [F2]; it is nonzero at $L(a)$ because $P\twoheadrightarrow L(a)\hookrightarrow P$ is nonzero. Induction on finite length, using the two short exact Hom sequences, gives the comparison for all sources and target $P$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 The unique maximal-weight Verma factor of $P$ lifts to an embedded $\Delta(\lambda)$ with Verma-filtered quotient. To see this, choose its position in a Verma flag. Earlier factors have no weights above $\lambda$ or at $\lambda$, so a lift of its highest vector is killed by $\mathfrak n^+$. The universal Verma map is injective because its composite to that flag factor is the identity. Its image splits that stage, and quotienting the full flag removes just this factor. Every Verma is annihilated by $C_+$ under the central action [F1], so $\Delta(\lambda)\subseteq K:=\{v\in P:C_+v=0\}$. If $K/\Delta(\lambda)\ne0$, it is a submodule of the Verma-filtered quotient; its socle contains $L(a)$ by the flag argument in step 1.1. Exactness of $V$ would give $\dim VK\ge2$, since $\dim V\Delta(\lambda)=1$. But inclusion into $P$ identifies $VK$ with a subspace of the one-dimensional socle of $VP=C$: every map $P\to K$ has image killed by $C_+$. This is impossible. Thus $K=\Delta(\lambda)$. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The comparison for target $P$ in step 2.1 intertwines the central action. Its subspace of maps annihilated by $C_+$ is exactly $\operatorname{Hom}(M,K)$ on the category-$\mathcal O$ side and $\operatorname{Hom}_C(VM,\operatorname{soc}C)$ on the module side. Step 2.2 and exactness identify these subspaces with $\operatorname{Hom}(M,\Delta(\lambda))$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_C(VM,V\Delta(\lambda))$. This proves the comparison for the dominant Verma without an invalid induction for merely left-exact functors. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 2.2]

[F4, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 1.2, algebra]

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let

[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image

   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra

facts: [F3] The genuine original-head Whittaker comparison is exact, identifies induced standards with their head-normalized finite Levi modules and scalar content central characters, sends standard-labelled simples to the distinct exhaustive finite-image simples and other simples to zero, and intertwines both ordinary tensor functors with V and V* and the actual right Casimir/flip operators; the standard-label crystal supplies predecessor head quotients, and the category-O detector contains every standard projective cover and has only standard labels in its head and socle ([[thm-skryabins-equivalence-for-the-type-a-whittaker-pair]], [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]]).

uses: 1.2 The exact ordinary-dual adjoint. For a finite rational $\mathfrak g$-module $E$, Skryabin transports ordinary evaluation $E^*\otimes E\to\mathbb C$ and coevaluation $\mathbb C\to E\otimes E^*$ to the tensor functors $F_E(M)=M\circledast E$. The ordinary zigzag identities give both adjunctions between $F_E$ and $F_{E^*}$. These functors are exact: tensoring is exact, it preserves generalized Whittaker modules by a finite Engel-flag nilpotence bound, and Skryabin is an exact equivalence. They preserve $\mathcal R_c$: a faithful finite image module embeds the regular algebra into a finite direct sum of copies of itself by evaluation on a basis, so every finite-image module is a subquotient of a finite sum of tensor modules; exact tensor transport sends degree $d$ to degree $d+1$. For $N>0$, also $V^*=\bigwedge^{N-1}V\otimes\det^{-1}$, and the exterior power is a summand of a tensor power by the antisymmetrizer. Determinant shifts therefore give closure under $V^*$ too. Consequently $F_V$ preserves projectives in the entire rational category through its exact right adjoint $F_{V^*}$. Here $V^*$ is the ordinary contragredient natural module, distinct from $V$; the transpose contravariant duality of category $\mathcal O$ is not this adjoint. [F3, construct, algebra]

4.1 Projectivity of the ground object. For $r\ge0$, take degree $Nr$ and the one-dimensional determinant-shifted ground object $D_r=\mathbb C_c\circledast\det^r$, with tableau $A_{c+r\mathbf1}$. Its content reconstructs it uniquely among column-strict tableaux: in each charge coset the minimum appears in every column and hence in its bottom box; removing these boxes and repeating reconstructs all columns. Therefore its scalar central-character summand has exactly this one simple, by F3. The regular-module multiplicity of $D_r$ is one. Indeed, the Levi decomposition of $Z_\nu$ uses semistandard tableaux of shapes given by the column partitions of ground differences, with the alphabet in column $j$ consisting of the terminal row boxes whose rows reach that column. This follows by expanding the complete symmetric characters of its symmetric factors and using the Schur semistandard formula, or successive horizontal-strip multiplication; its finite radical filtration makes it an actual $\mathfrak p$-filtration by these Levi sections. For $D_r$ the shapes are rectangles $(r^{q_j})$ and the allowed alphabet has exactly $q_j$ letters. Each length-$q_j$ strictly increasing tableau column must contain every letter in order. There is exactly one tuple, and its row-$i$ multiplicity is $rp_i$. Thus the coefficient is one for $\nu_i=rp_i$ and zero for every other occupancy. Other standards cannot contain $D_r$ because their scalar central characters differ. The supported regular summand has length one and is $D_r$ itself, so $D_r$ is projective over $W_{Nr}$. For a surjection in the rational finite-W category $\mathcal R_c$, a common determinant twist puts its terms into finite sums of polynomial-image categories. The scalar degree operator splits these by degree. A map from $\mathbb C_c$ becomes a map from $D_r$ into the degree-$Nr$ summand, where it lifts by the projectivity just proved. The inverse determinant twist gives the original lift. Hence $\mathbb C_c$ is projective in $\mathcal R_c$, without claiming projectivity in arbitrary $W(\lambda)$-mod. 5.1 The finite-W projective covers. Put $Q(A)=\operatorname{Wh}(P(A))$ for standard labels. At degree zero this is the ground object, projective by step 4.1. Lifting along the projective cover and splitting proves $P(A)$ is a summand of $P(B)\otimes V$. The genuine tensor comparison sends this to a summand of $Q(B)\circledast V$, projective by step 1.2. To identify its head, write $P(B)\otimes V=\bigoplus_C P(C)^{m_C}$ with standard $C$, using the independently proved detector head/socle property in F3. 2.1 **Actual standard embeddings.** Given $C$, shift columns $j\ge2$ upward by integers $k_j\ge0$, chosen successively so each shifted entry in column $j$ exceeds every earlier-column entry in its coset. In each elementary standard flag, alternative valid lowers occur in earlier columns, hence have strictly smaller prefix Bruhat label. Our desired section is largest and can be moved to the bottom: each adjacent swap splits by the Ext ordering in [F2]. 2.2 **An actual cover isomorphism.** Append the ground last column to $B'$. Every $C\ge B$ retains that ground column: a same-coset Bruhat move toward a larger label increases earlier-column sums, so the last-column sum cannot exceed its ground sum, whereas polynomiality makes each last-column entry at least its ground value. Equality forces all of them to be ground; admissibility excludes cross-coset swaps. Thus all $C\ge B$ have degree split $(d',0)$. By BGG and step 1.2 their standard-flag multiplicities agree in the fixed split and vanish elsewhere. The kernel of this existing epimorphism therefore has every composition multiplicity zero and is zero. Consequently $X\cong P(B)$; an equality of characters has only been used to kill the kernel of an already constructed map. [F2, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 **The detector and the injective hulls it contains.** The ground simple is projective-injective. Tensoring by $V$ preserves both projectives and injectives because the distinct tensor functor $-\otimes V^*$ is exact and adjoint on both sides. The tensor product contravariant form gives $T\cong DT$. Every simple submodule of a standard-filtered object embeds in one of its successive standard sections, by taking the first section meeting it; hence step 2.1 proves standard socle for every projective and for $T$. Duality gives standard head for $T$. Every standard label of positive degree is $\widetilde f_iB$ for a lower-degree standard label by [F3]; induction using the actual crystal head of $f_iL(B)$ gives $T\twoheadrightarrow L(A)$. Lift this epimorphism through $P(A)\twoheadrightarrow L(A)$; essentiality makes the lift surjective and projectivity splits it. Thus the indecomposable summands of $T$ are exactly the standard-labelled covers, all with positive multiplicity and all injective. Moreover $I(A)=DP(A)\in\operatorname{add}(DT)=\operatorname{add}(T)$ for every standard $A$. This hull membership does not presume individual summand self-duality. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

Removing the last column and using tensor identity gives $Z(A,c)=R(Z(A',c')\boxtimes\mathbb C_{c_l+q_l-n})\otimes\bigotimes_{i=N-q_l+1}^{N}\operatorname{Sym}^{a_i}(V)$. By induction and step 2.2 the first factor is a sum of actual projective covers. The remaining finite tensor product preserves projectives by its exact distinct-dual adjoint. Polynomial labels form whole blocks: their shared entry multiset cannot admit a below-ground entry, since column strictness would put an entry below the common coset minimum in the bottom row. Thus these ambient projectives lie in the required finite polynomial summand. Every $Z(A,c)$ is genuinely projective. [F2, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 **Every cover occurs and the quotient has a standard flag.** For a label $B$, take $A=B-A_c$. Project each prefix onto its last-column Levi quotient. The tensor product of the resulting row symmetric powers surjects onto $V(B)$: row symmetrization followed by column antisymmetrization of the row-filled tensor produces a nonzero polynomial highest vector, and Levi complete reducibility gives the simple Schur quotient. Exact induction gives $Z(A,c)\twoheadrightarrow N(B)\twoheadrightarrow L(B)$, and projectivity plus essentiality of the cover makes $P(B)$ a split summand of $Z(A,c)$. Averaging symmetrizers embed $Z_A$ as a $\mathfrak p$-submodule of $V^{\otimes d}$; PBW preserves this injection and identifies the ambient induction with $T$. Its finite $\mathfrak p$-quotient has polynomial Levi simple sections: the radical acts nilpotently by the column filtration, and its invariant subspace in each simple section is Levi-stable and therefore the whole section. Inducing its composition filtration exactly gives a standard flag of $T/Z(A,c)$. [F2, step 3.2, construct, algebra]

5.1 **All-projective copresentations.** For an indecomposable projective $P$, choose a splitting $Z(A,c)=P\oplus Q$ from step 4.1 and view $P$ as its actual submodule of $T$. The sequence $0\to Q\to T/P\to T/Z(A,c)\to0$ gives a standard flag of $T/P$, since $Q$ is projective and has its BGG flag. Its socle is standard by step 2.1, so its finite injective hull $I(T/P)$ belongs to $\operatorname{add}(T)$ by step 3.1. Compose $T\twoheadrightarrow T/P\hookrightarrow I(T/P)$ to obtain $0\to P\to T\to I(T/P)$, exact at $P,T$. Finite sums give every projective a two-step copresentation $0\to P\to T_0\to T_1$ with both $T_i\in\operatorname{add}(T)$. The last arrow need not be surjective. [F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 **The right-adjoint unit.** Choose a full finite projective generator of the entire category-O summand containing $T$ as an explicit summand, with algebra $A$, and let $e$ be the projector onto this actual $T$. Thus $eAe=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$, retaining all its multiplicities. For $F(X)=eX$, $B=eAe$, the right adjoint is $G_e(M)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(eA,M)$ with unit $\eta_X(x)(ea)=eax$. The restriction $e\eta_X$ is an isomorphism, so its kernel and cokernel are annihilated by $e$. If $X$ has standard socle then $\eta_X$ is monic. In particular $\eta_T$ is monic and splits since its source $T$ is injective. A complementary summand $C$ has $eC=0$, but adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,G_eFT)=\operatorname{Hom}_B(eC,FT)=0$, forcing its inclusion to vanish and $C=0$. Thus $\eta$ is an isomorphism on $\operatorname{add}(T)$. Apply exact $F$ and left-exact $G_e$ to step 5.1; the comparison of kernels gives $\eta_P$ an isomorphism for every projective. Adjunction therefore proves $F$ fully faithful on all projectives, while left-adjoint recovery has only been asserted on $\operatorname{add}(T)$. [F2, step 3.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 **Tilting full faithfulness.** If $X$ has standard head and $Y$ standard socle, then $\eta_Y$ is monic and its cokernel is annihilated by $e$. Every map from $X$ to that cokernel vanishes: a nonzero image would have a standard simple head because it is a quotient of $X$, while all its factors would be off-standard. By adjunction each $B$-map $FX\to FY$ gives $X\to G_eFY$, which therefore factors uniquely through $Y$. This proves the Hom isomorphism. A tilting's standard flag gives standard socle by step 2.1, and its costandard flag gives standard head by duality. Thus the quotient is fully faithful on all tiltings. [F2, step 2.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 **The actual Whittaker comparison and quotient.** By [F1] the exact Whittaker functor factors through $F$ as the actual equivalence $U\otimes_B-$, with $U$ a right $B$-progenerator and $W_d=\operatorname{End}_B(U)$. Its inverse is $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,-)$, and its unit on $FX$ is $m\mapsto(u\mapsto u\otimes m)$. Under the source action this is precisely $\gamma_X(f)=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}(f)j^{-1}$, since the counit on $T\otimes_B FX$ is evaluation; thus the comparison is a natural isomorphism of actual maps and Hecke modules. In particular $U$ is a left $W_d$-progenerator, and $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$ is fully faithful on projectives by step 6.1. The corner functor $F$ is the Serre quotient with kernel consisting of objects with only off-standard factors; applying the genuine equivalence identifies the same quotient for $V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}$. Projectivity is preserved on $\operatorname{add}(T)$, whose image consists of the corresponding projective covers. This does not assert preservation for other ambient projectives. [F1, step 3.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra]

9.1 **Simple images and standard heads.** The exact corner functor kills precisely off-standard simples and identifies its other simple images with the distinct exhaustive $B$-simples; the genuine equivalence of step 8.1 transports these to the corresponding finite-W simples $L_W(A)$. For standard $A$, $P(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$, so $\pi P(A)$ is an indecomposable $B$-projective with head $\pi L(A)$: its Hom to each simple is the corresponding Hom from $P(A)$ by the elementary add$(T)$ equivalence. Lift $P(A)\to L(A)$ through $N(A)\to L(A)$; the image surjects onto the standard's head and is therefore the whole standard. Applying exact $\pi$ makes $\pi N(A)$ a nonzero quotient of this indecomposable projective, so it has the same unique simple head. Through Morita, the actual finite-Levi standard $V(A)=V_{\!\mathrm{Wh}}N(A)$ likewise has unique simple head $L_W(A)$. This does not assert that a specified finite-Levi highest vector generates it. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 8.1, algebra]

9.2 **Independent row compression.** Add $t$ full ground rows until the enlarged smallest column has height at least $d$; all roots $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ remain fixed. For each row $r$, the normalized coefficient $D_r^{(1)}$ is its row-Cartan operator, with ground scalar $\kappa_r=\sum_{j:\,r\text{ lies in column }j}c_j$. On the actual tensor space and every finite-Levi standard of degree $d$ its eigenvalues are $\kappa_r+h$, $0\le h\le d$, since the remaining weight is polynomial row occupancy. Thus the SAME finite-image element $e=\prod_{r\text{ deleted}}\prod_{h=1}^{d}(1-(D_r^{(1)}-\kappa_r)/h)$ is the zero-deleted-occupancy projector on both tensor space and all these standards. In $U^+$ it selects tensors using only retained rows. The actual dot formula preserves row multisets, so $e$ commutes with dots and crossings and belongs to the left image by the independent raw first centralizer of [F1]. Each right matrix restricts identically under the retained-box embedding: left neighbours and row/column indices agree and its scalar $a_j$ is unchanged. Therefore $eU^+=U$ as right Hecke modules. Extending a commuting endomorphism of $eU^+$ by zero shows $eA^+e=A$, where $A^+,A$ are the large and small left image algebras. For the finite-Levi standard, the zero-deleted-occupancy part of $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j+t})$ is $\mathbb C_{c_j}\otimes S_{\mu^{(j)}}(\mathbb C^{q_j})$ by its tensor Young-symmetrizer realization, and vanishes exactly when a deleted-row partition entry is nonzero. In the original path expansion, Levi projection kills off-column factors and each surviving strictly-forward path has at most one factor in each column. A deleted intermediate row changes removed-coordinate occupancy in a column with no later factor there to undo it; compression therefore kills that monomial. Remaining paths are exactly the small paths. The head shift in column $j$ changes by $-(j-1)t$, cancelling the retained source-reading shift $+(j-1)t$; its normalized highest weight remains the entry plus row index minus one. The corner action and its Gauss coefficients consequently give $eV(A^+)=V(A)$ for contractible labels and zero for noncontractible labels, as actual module identifications. [F1, F2, F4, step 8.1, construct, algebra]

10.1 **Simple contraction without highest-vector assumptions.** Every noncontractible standard simple is killed by $e$, because it is a quotient of the standard annihilated in step 9.2. For a finite algebra and an idempotent $e$, restriction gives a bijection between its simple modules surviving $e$ and the simples of $eAe$: any nonzero vector in $eL$ generates $eL=eAe v$, and for a small simple $M$ the module $Ae\otimes_{eAe}M$ has a unique simple quotient surviving $e$. Indeed its $e$-part is $M$; every proper submodule has zero $e$-part, since a submodule containing that part generates the whole induced module. The sum of all such proper submodules is still annihilated by $e$ and is the unique maximal submodule. Apply this to the independent corner in step 9.2. By step 9.1 both simple lists are complete, and small standard labels are in bijection with contractible large standard labels by adjoining full ground rows. Thus the survivors form a subset of the contractible list with exactly the same finite cardinality, so every contractible simple survives. Its restriction is a simple quotient of $eV(A^+)=V(A)$, which has the unique head from step 9.1, hence $eL_W(A^+)=L_W(A)$. [F1, step 9.1, step 9.2, construct, algebra]

11.1 **Fullness and the central Hecke corner.** If a contractible $A^+$ and another label have the same entry-multiset central character, admissibility separates charge cosets and identifies all charges within each coset. Its minimal bottom entry $c_j+1-(n+t)$ appears in each column of that coset; strictness and nonnegative ground differences force the same entries into the bottom row of the other label. Remove that row and repeat for every deleted row. Thus the contractible labels form a union of whole central-character blocks. Let $f$ be their central support in $A^+$; then $e=ef=fe$, since $e$ kills all complementary simples. Every simple of $A_f=fA^+f$ survives $e$ by step 10.1. If $A_feA_f$ were proper, its nonzero quotient would have a simple killed by $e$, a contradiction. Hence $f=\sum_k a_keb_k$. Multiplication $A_fe\otimes_{eA_fe}eM\to M$ has inverse $m\mapsto\sum_k a_ke\otimes eb_km$; balancing and this identity verify both composites. This gives a faithful Morita equivalence on all supported-block modules. The operator $f$ belongs to the right centralizer and is central there, so restriction identifies $fB^+f=\operatorname{End}_{A_f}(fU^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $B=\operatorname{End}_{eA_fe}(eU^+)^{\mathrm{op}}$. To verify enlarged stable faithfulness directly, choose $d$ distinct terminal boxes on length-$l$ Jordan strings. In the associated graded tensor action each bounded PBW word $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_d^{a_d}w$, $0\le a_i<l$, sends their ordered terminal tensor to the tensor in which those distinct strings have been permuted by $w$ and the box on string $i$ moved $a_i$ places left. These $l^dd!$ outputs are distinct basis tensors, so the graded PBW word images are linearly independent. A nonzero filtered Hecke element has a nonzero leading PBW symbol; graded injectivity makes its leading operator nonzero, hence its actual operator is nonzero. The enlarged stable action is therefore faithful, giving $B=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$. Its trace is therefore symmetric and nondegenerate by [F4]. This local proof precedes, and does not depend on, a later stable-range definition. [F1, F2, F4, step 9.2, step 10.1, construct, algebra]

12.1 **The actual duality comparison.** Let $\beta:T\to DT$ be the tensor contravariant form. Put $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T)$ with $(bf)(m)=f(m)b^*$, and $X^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{B}(X,B)$ with the same twist. Transposition gives the natural isomorphism $\delta M\to\pi DM$, $f\mapsto Df\circ\beta$, whose inverse is $g\mapsto\beta^{-1}\circ Dg\circ\operatorname{bidual}_M$. This uses only $T\cong DT$, not individual projective self-duality. Tensor-Hom gives $\delta\pi^*\cong\#$, and the symmetric trace of step 11.1 gives $\#\cong D_B$ by $h\mapsto\operatorname{tr}\circ h$. Define $\theta_M:M\to D\pi^*\delta M$ by $\theta_M(m)(t\otimes f)=(t,f(m))$. The form identity $(xtb,t')=(t,x^{\mathrm{tr}}t'b^*)$ makes this balanced and $\mathfrak g$-linear. Applying $\pi$ gives a natural map $\pi\to\pi D\pi^*\delta\cong\#\pi D$ between exact functors; exactness of $\#$ follows from the symmetric algebra's injective regular module. On $T$ it is the regular trace-duality isomorphism, and hence is invertible on add$(T)$. Use the copresentations of step 5.1 and kernels to prove it invertible on every projective; use finite projective presentations and cokernels to prove it invertible on every object. Dualizing gives the genuine module isomorphism $\pi D\cong D_B\pi$. [F2, F4, step 5.1, step 11.1, construct, algebra]

13.1 **Individual standard prinjectives are self-dual.** For standard $A$, $I(A)=DP(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$ by step 3.1. Step 12.1 gives $\pi I(A)=D_B\pi P(A)$ and fixes its simple label because $DL(A)=L(A)$. In a symmetric algebra the primitive projective $Be_A$ is also the injective hull of its corresponding simple: the perfect trace identifies its linear dual with the corresponding right ideal, and the $*$ twist sends the primitive to the primitive carrying the dual simple. Since that simple is fixed here, $D_B\pi P(A)\cong\pi P(A)$. Both $I(A)$ and $P(A)$ are projectives, so full faithfulness of step 6.1 lifts this isomorphism and its inverse; their composites are identities by faithfulness. Hence $I(A)\cong P(A)$, so each standard projective-injective is individually self-dual. This last conclusion has been derived after the copresentation, central-corner and duality constructions, and was not used to prove them. [F2, step 3.1, step 6.1, step 12.1, algebra] ∎

opposite **highest-weight Serre quotient** by the complementary labels (an upper

facts: [F2] Tilting classification ([[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]], [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]]): uniqueness/maximal support, $T(A)$ with $M(A)$ once at the bottom, restricted duality fixing tiltings, and lower-ideal invariance.

uses: 2.1 **Actual projective-to-tilting transport.** Put $X(A)=\Psi(\bar P(A))$. In the source highest-weight block the labelled projective has an exact sequence $0\to\bar K(A)\to\bar P(A)\to\bar\Delta(A)\to0$, with $\bar K(A)$ standard-filtered by labels strictly above $A$. The exact contravariant equivalence $\Psi$ turns it into $0\to\Delta(A)\to X(A)\to\Psi\bar K(A)\to0$; the reversed label order makes the quotient standard-filtered by labels strictly below $A$. 4.1 **Full blocks and proper ideals.** Since both filtered equivalences are fully faithful, the endomorphism ring of the opposite projective generator equals that of the characteristic tilting generator, so the full-block Ringel dual is the opposite-parabolic block. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1]

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a regular integral block and simple reflection
$s$, with $C=\operatorname{End}(P(w_0\cdot\lambda))$, there is a natural
isomorphism of functors to left $C$-modules
$$V\theta_s\cong C\otimes_{C^s}V.$$
Equivalently the functor is tensoring by the $(C,C)$-bimodule
$C\otimes_{C^s}C$, with left action on the first factor and right action on the
second. In type A over $\mathbb C$, its polynomial lift is tensoring on the
left by $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$; read up to the auxiliary suspension
normalisation fixed by the rank-one case, the right origin reduction of $B_s$
is the two-dimensional module of centered degrees $-1,1$, for $M=S$ the
coinvariant reduction satisfies
$B_s\otimes_SC\cong(C\otimes_{C^s}C)(1)$ in the same normalisation, and
$B_s\otimes_S\mathbb C$ itself is not the bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$: the
former has vector-space dimension two, whereas the latter has dimension
$2|W|$. Forgetting the grading gives the displayed category-$\mathcal O$
formula, and no grading on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is asserted.
